testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: The ____ shows a driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: A driver can stay alert by:

options.text: Not wearing sunglasses during the day.
Having another person ride with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Having another person ride with them.
questions.explanation: To stay alert while driving, wear sunglasses to reduce eye strain, keep the cab cool, avoid heavy foods, and travel with someone who can help with driving duties.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air pressure pushes out the rod and moves the:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: When it is hard to see, such as at dawn or dusk, what is the best way to make your vehicle more visible?
questions.explanation: When visibility is poor (at dawn, dusk, in rain, or in snow), turn on your low beam headlights. This makes your vehicle easier to see. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: If your coolant level is low, you should:
questions.explanation: Check the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid level regularly. Your engine needs enough coolant in both cold and hot weather.

questions.question: Windshield wiper blades should be:
questions.explanation: When you inspect your vehicle, check the wiper blades for damage and stiff rubber. Make sure they are secure and clean.

questions.question: On newer vehicles, how do you set the parking brake?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.
Push in the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pull up on the steering column.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
questions.explanation: On newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake has a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob out to set the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: Cargo on flatbed trailers should be:
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers or trailers without sides, cargo must be tied down so it does not shift or fall off during transport.

questions.question: Seat belts:

options.text: Are optional for those holding a CDL.
Are required, but only if a driver is transporting hazardous materials.
Are required to be used by all drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required to be used by all drivers.
questions.explanation: You must wear a seat belt at all times while driving a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: If a vehicle has a vehicle inspection report, the driver should:

options.text: Not look at the report and find any issues themselves.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and rely only on the report.

questions.explanation: Start your vehicle inspection by reviewing the last inspection report if one exists. The carrier should have fixed any problems noted in the report.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other vehicles with air brakes built after March 1, 1998 also must have ABS.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how does it affect your braking distance?
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase braking distance. When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, your braking distance multiplies by four.

questions.question: A pre-trip vehicle inspection:

options.text: Is not required if you use the vehicle regularly.
Is not required for trips under 100 miles.
Must only be done by a mechanic.

questions.explanation: State and federal law require drivers to inspect their vehicles before driving.

questions.question: When traction is poor, a driver should accelerate slowly to:

options.text: Be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.explanation: Accelerating too quickly on slippery roads can cause you to lose control of your vehicle. When traction is poor, accelerate slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: When checking your brakes, the slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from the push rod attachment point.
questions.explanation: Set wheel chocks and disengage the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to check movement. It should not move more than one inch from the push rod. Movement beyond one inch means it needs adjustment.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving is:

options.text: Not helpful since you cannot control what is far away.
Only needed when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to see hazards and respond safely.

questions.question: Test your low pressure warning signal:
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light is critical for safety. Let the system charge, then test it by quickly applying and releasing the brake pedal. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: Headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam whenever it is safe and legal.

questions.correctAnswerText: On high beam whenever it is safe and legal.
questions.explanation: Use high beams at night to improve visibility when safe and legal. However, switch to low beams when you are within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle to avoid blinding other drivers.

questions.question: Which is NOT a driving hazard?

options.text: A police car on the roadside

questions.explanation: Accidents distract drivers and involve people not watching traffic. Ice cream trucks attract children who ignore passing vehicles. An open road presents no hazard.

questions.question: Non-front tires on a commercial vehicle must have a minimum tread depth of:
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Non-front tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread depth. All tires on the same vehicle must be the same size.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate allowed for a triple combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: You need to know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle should lose no more than 6 psi per minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is tailgating you?
questions.explanation: If you are being tailgated, increase the space in front of your vehicle. This helps you avoid sudden stops that could cause a crash. It also makes it easier for the other driver to pass. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a distracted driver on the road?
questions.explanation: Give a distracted driver plenty of space. Be careful if you pass them because they may not see you and could drift into your lane.

questions.question: What should a driver do if a tire fails?

options.text: Keep one hand on the wheel and wave to other drivers with the other hand

questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Unless you must brake to avoid danger, stay off the brakes until your vehicle slows down. Then brake gently, pull off the road, and stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distracted person that motorists should worry about?

options.text: A person talking to another person in their vehicle
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people who are not paying attention to traffic. Watch out for drivers talking to passengers, children near the road, and road workers.

questions.question: How can you use less braking on a downhill stretch of road?
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going down a hill. This helps your vehicle stay at a safe speed without needing heavy braking.

questions.question: Where should a helper stand when backing a vehicle?

options.text: In front of the passenger side
In front of the driver side
On the side of the truck
Near the back of the truck

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the truck
questions.explanation: Your helper should stand near the back of the vehicle where you can see them. Before backing up, agree on hand signals with your helper. Make sure you both understand the signal for "stop."

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, the air compressor must build to at least ____ psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to reach at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out and call for help
Keep trying to remove the vehicle from the tracks
Walk down the tracks to look for a train

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and call for help
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, exit immediately and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency services right away.

questions.question: When driving, what should a driver pay attention to?

options.text: Not the right side of their vehicle
Not in front of their vehicle

questions.explanation: A commercial driver must stay aware of everything happening around their vehicle on all sides.

questions.question: What should you do if fog covers the roadway?
questions.explanation: Fog makes driving dangerous. If you can, do not drive in foggy conditions.

questions.question: What equipment must a commercial motor vehicle have?

options.text: A fire extinguisher only if transporting hazardous materials.
A fire extinguisher only if traveling through remote areas.
At least one fire extinguisher at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least one fire extinguisher at all times.
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes at least one fire extinguisher, spare fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for when the vehicle is parked.

questions.question: Where is the tire load rating located?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door
On the side of each tire

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire
questions.explanation: The tire load rating shows the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a certain pressure. This number is written on the side of each tire.

questions.question: What should you do when parked on the side of the road?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: When stopped on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is very important at night.

questions.question: Which crime would NOT disqualify someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Several crimes will disqualify someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. These include kidnapping, smuggling, and immigration violations. More serious crimes like murder result in a lifetime ban.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one system leaks, what happens?

options.text: The other system may not be affected.
The other system will also be affected.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other system may not be affected.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other.

questions.question: Which is NOT a suspension system defect?
questions.explanation: Suspension problems include cracked or broken spring hangers, missing or broken leaves in a leaf spring, and leaking shock absorbers. Have these repaired if found.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: To keep other drivers away from you.
To alert other drivers that you are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: To alert other drivers that you are nearby.
questions.explanation: Your horn warns other road users that you are there. Only use it when necessary, as it could startle another driver and cause danger.

questions.question: Where are the ABS malfunction lamps on trucks and buses?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle by the passenger's door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with Anti-Lock Braking Systems have yellow warning lights on the instrument panel. Trailers have yellow ABS lights on the left side, on the front or rear corner.

questions.question: What should you do when turning to avoid a hazard?

options.text: Do not brake, as it could lock the wheels.
Hold down the brakes until you pass the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake, as it could lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes while turning to avoid a hazard. Braking while turning can lock the wheels and cause a skid.

questions.question: When backing up, what is best to do?

options.text: Use only the passenger's side mirror.
Turn toward the passenger's side when you can.
Have someone help you if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have someone help you if possible.
questions.explanation: Back up slowly and check both side mirrors. Use a helper to watch your blind spots. You and the helper should agree on a signal that means "stop."

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Let rain water enter the air tanks.
Remove water and oil from air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains that remove water and compressor oil. If these liquids build up, they damage the air brake system.

questions.question: What must be on an air tank in an air-braked vehicle?
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be between the air compressor and the first tank. It stops air from leaking out if the compressor breaks.

questions.question: How can you stay awake on a long trip?

options.text: Sleep for only three hours before driving.
Plan your trip and schedule rest stops.
Skip exercise in your daily routine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip and schedule rest stops.
questions.explanation: Sleep seven to eight hours before driving. Drive during hours when you are normally awake. Take breaks during the trip. Exercise regularly.

questions.question: If a tire fails, what should you do?

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Check your tires after the vehicle stops completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your tires after the vehicle stops completely.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly. Do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. When it slows enough, brake gently and pull off the road. Then check your tires.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: Drains water and compressor oil from air tanks.
Stops air from leaking out if the compressor breaks.
Activates emergency brakes when there is a leak.
Holds spring brakes in place until they are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from leaking out if the compressor breaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is between the air compressor and the first tank. It keeps air from escaping if the compressor has a leak.

questions.question: Where are emergency brakes required?
questions.explanation: Trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must work by mechanical force.

questions.question: How should you park to leave safely?

options.text: So you must back up to leave.
So you can pull forward to leave.
On the side of a roadway, not in a parking lot.
By backing into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can pull forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous. Park so you can pull forward to exit your space.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park a vehicle with air brakes.

questions.question: When making a turn, what do you NOT need to do?

options.text: Turn off your turn signal after the turn.
Signal the whole time you are turning.

questions.explanation: Turn on your signal early. Keep it on during the entire turn. Turn it off after the turn is complete.
